Found by the pre-cutover config audit (2026-08-09, read-only, source at wip head f673299). CUTOVER-BLOCKER.

## The gap
- scripts/local-clone.ts:31 pins the dogfood clone to server/main.ts.
- package.json:8-9: core01 runs `bun run src/index.ts` (start) / scripts/run-two-worker.ts (start:two-worker), and run-two-worker.ts:50 spawns `bun run src/index.ts` per worker.
- `rg -c "createCaptureHealthRuntime|CAPTURE_HEALTH" src/index.ts` → 0. server/main.ts → 2.

So the entire capture-health chain merged tonight — observer, /health capture block, the required-namespace WARN at server/main.ts:273, and by extension the value of #659/#661's launcher key fixes — is absent from the tree core01 actually runs. Setting OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_* on core01 reads nothing.

## Failure scenario
Set OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_NAMESPACE on core01, deploy, curl /health, see no capture block, misdiagnose as an allowlist drop (#659's shape) and hunt an allowlist that isn't on this path. The code simply is not there.

## This is a known repo pattern
docs/sme/correctness.md:1822 — "TWO serving trees... a cross-cutting install done on only one leaves the other tree's call sites permanently inert." PR #599 shipped this exact class once.

## Wanted (operator decision required — do NOT pick silently)
Either (a) cut core01 over to server/main.ts as its entrypoint, or (b) port the capture-health runtime composition into src/index.ts. This is an architecture decision about which tree is canonical, not a lane's to choose. Whichever: a done-means check must assert the capture block is live on the core01 serving tree (feature-signal, not revision), and the two-serving-trees SME entry gets a regression note. Truth grammar: WRITTEN in server/, NOT in the core01 serving path.
